response.rationale: Renal phosphate wasting with hypophosphatemia, elevated 1,25(OH)2D, suppressed PTH, undetectable FGF23, and nephrocalcinosis best fit hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria, despite the atypical normal urine calcium. Other candidates are contradicted by the FGF23/1,25/PTH pattern.

rejected.why: X-linked hypophosphatemia is FGF23-mediated; undetectable FGF23 and elevated 1,25(OH)2D with low PTH directly contradict it.
Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1A causes low 1,25(OH)2D and secondary hyperparathyroidism, opposite of the elevated 1,25 and low PTH seen here.
Fibrous dysplasia does not explain elevated 1,25(OH)2D, low PTH, undetectable FGF23, or nephrocalcinosis; hypophosphatemia in fibrous dysplasia is typically FGF23-mediated.
